$comment: Every concurrency site in the pipeline's non-test Rust, with the documented pattern it follows (docs/concurrency.md, "The patterns") and why. Checked by scripts/concurrency-census.ts (gate stage census:concurrency, and pre-commit on staged .rs). Key = file + scope (enclosing fn or item) + construct; no line numbers. `exception` marks a known deviation from the doc's rules and names the open finding. Seeded 2026-10-12 from the audit (docs/audits/rust-concurrency-2026-10.md).

`kill -KILL -- -<pgid>` on the timeout path (core forbids unsafe, so no kill(2)): kill(1) returns at once and needs no deadline of its own; stdio null; whether it worked is reported in TimedOut.killed
one bounded sync_channel (capacity 4, one slot per sender) carries the threads' events; nobody blocks on a send. A disconnect with events missing (a drain panicked) kills the group and is an error
stdout and stderr always piped (stdin only when there is input): each pipe has its own drain thread, so no write can block on a full pipe (audit W1)

the drains, the stdin feeder and the exit waiter: plain threads on purpose (not scoped) — if something outside the killed process group still holds a pipe, they end when it closes and the run does not wait on them. Each sends exactly one event and exits; nothing they produce reaches output except through the returned Finished
recv_timeout until ONE deadline from before spawn: it covers stdin, both outputs and the exit together (rule 3); on expiry the process group is SIGKILLed and the caller gets TimedOut

the webcrack shim (audit W1 + follow-up, fixed): through crate::subprocess::run, which feeds stdin while both outputs drain, under WebcrackShim::deadline (production WEBCRACK_DEADLINE, 30 min vs 12 s measured on a 2.9 MB webpack bundle); a timeout kills the shim's process group; timeout, non-zero exit or unparseable output is an error

the offline index builder's work queue: one Mutex<usize> taken for an increment to claim the next task index, one Mutex<Vec> for a push of a failed task's error; neither is held across a task. The errors are sorted before they are returned, so completion order never reaches output

the offline index builder (humanify-index, not the pipeline) runs at most cfg.jobs.clamp(1, 4) package tasks at once — each an npm install plus bundler builds, subprocess-bound, every one under its own deadline — on scoped threads joined before return. Each task writes only its own shard files; the merge reads them in plan order, so completion order never reaches the index

`npm install --before=<publish date>` of one package (retried once with --legacy-peer-deps), through humanify_core::subprocess::run under INSTALL_DEADLINE (30 min; tens of seconds in the exp095 builds); a failure or timeout fails the task, which writes no shard and is reported as FAILED

`<bundler> --version` (`node <recipe script> --version` for webpack and rollup, exp105) for the index manifest, built here and run by bundler_version through humanify_core::subprocess::run under VERSION_DEADLINE (1 min; it answers in ms); a non-zero exit, empty answer or timeout is an error

one minified bun/esbuild build (or `node <recipe script>` for webpack and rollup, exp105) of a package entry, built here and run by RecipeBuild::build through humanify_core::subprocess::run under BUILD_DEADLINE (30 min; seconds in the exp095 builds); a non-zero exit or timeout returns the error text and the build contributes no files (the module shard records it)

`npm view <name> time versions --json` for a packument not yet cached, through humanify_core::subprocess::run under VIEW_DEADLINE (5 min; seconds); a non-zero exit, timeout or unparseable JSON is an error naming the package

entries.reason: exp154 run-time index machinery: the WAIT_DEADLINE expired, so the join sets the stop flag (SeqCst) and the build halts at its next task boundary; the flag gates nothing else and no output depends on its ordering

the joint: one recv_timeout over the whole wait (WAIT_DEADLINE, 90 min), then a STOP_GRACE recv for the build's final word once the stop flag is set — every subprocess the build runs is itself deadline'd and stop is checked between tasks, so the grace is guaranteed; a miss panics (a bug), never an unbounded wait

exp154: a bounded mpsc::sync_channel(1) carrying the job's ONE answer to the joint; a closed channel (the run failed before it took the answer) is a decided outcome — the thread exits, the answer is dropped, nothing silently retries
exp154: the run's stop flag, handed to the job thread so an expired wait (or a failed run) halts the build at its next task boundary; a pure halt signal, nothing that decides output reads it
exp154: bounded sync_channel(1) for the job's single answer; the sender blocks at most until the joint takes it under its deadline, a closed channel ends the thread
exp154: the job checks the stop flag (SeqCst) once before it starts — a run that already failed never launches a build; a pure halt signal

exp154: the two noticeboard Mutexes handed to the build's Trace (current stage name, stage→wall-ms map) — taken briefly to write one string / bump one counter, never held across a subprocess or any call; the same locks build.rs's Trace::stage takes

exp154: the run's stop flag for the index machinery — set when the run fails before it takes the job's answer (the scope's join then waits at most one in-flight subprocess, never the build's deadline) and by the joint itself on expiry

exp154: the store search / run-time build runs on a scoped thread so it overlaps the run's prior load and dispatch setup; it is never detached — the scope cannot end before the library load has taken the answer through the deadline'd joint, and thread::scope joins it there
exp154: the joint takes the run's stop flag to wait on the machinery's answer (and to set it if the wait deadline expires); nothing that decides output races on it
exp154: Trace.stop — the flag a deadline'd caller sets; the build loads it (SeqCst) between tasks only, a pure halt signal
exp154: Trace.stage / Trace.stages — the caller's noticeboards (current stage name, stage→wall-ms map); taken briefly per stage boundary, never held across the stage's own work
exp154: the stage guard takes the stage-name Mutex on drop to write one string; a RAII boundary write, nothing else
